title: Empirical Evaluation of a Validator‑Assisted LLM NetOps Pipeline: A Paired Study with gpt-5‑mini on 400 Intent→Configuration Tasks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (CAND‑2026‑002) measuring operational failure outcomes for LLM‑generated configuration changes and the effect of a lightweight deterministic validator (with at most one deterministic LLM repair call). Using gpt‑5‑mini via a hosted NetOps adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) on 400 unique public/synthetic intents (paired Baseline=Direct‑apply vs Guarded=validator+≤1 repair) in sandboxed emulator replicas, we observed no operational failures in either arm (n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The paired difference (Guarded − Baseline) = 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI 0.00–0.00, 10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.0. Crucially, the preregistered generation semantics used a single shared initial candidate per intent (independent_condition_generation=false), so Guarded could only differ if the validator rejected that shared candidate and a repair call produced an accepted alternative. In this run the validator issued 0 rejects and 0 repair calls. We therefore report a reproducible boundary case and release full preregistration, execution, scoring, and analysis artifacts (paths and hashes recorded in the execution manifest). We carefully bound interpretation: these results document behavior under the documented task distribution, model, adapter, and shared‑candidate protocol, and do not imply general production safety or validator ineffectiveness. We discuss limitations, threats to validity, and concrete next steps that follow from the archived artifacts.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being proposed to convert high‑level operator intent into low‑level device configurations (intent→configuration) and to assist NetOps workflows (synthesis, remediation, limited self‑healing). Operational adoption requires evidence about realistic failure rates and about the marginal benefit of lightweight automated validators and bounded repair loops. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑002 to measure: What is the paired difference in operational failure proportion when applying LLM‑generated changes directly (Baseline) versus applying a deterministic validator plus at most one deterministic LLM repair (Guarded)? We emphasize three design priorities mandated by the preregistration: (i) transparent archival of every prompt/output/tool call and SHA‑256 hash (see execution_manifest), (ii) a preregistered paired analysis using McNemar and bootstrap inference, and (iii) a minimal bounded repair budget (≤1 repair call) to model a lightweight automated validation pipeline. Contributions: (1) machine‑readable preregistration and full execution artifacts; (2) a fully executed paired run (400 intents, 800 episodes) using gpt‑5‑mini and adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1; (3) a transparent report of the observed boundary case (zero validator interventions) with artifact‑grounded interpretation and threats to validity.
sections.related_work: Prior work spans intent‑driven NetOps and generation→validate→repair pipelines. Surveys and recent studies motivate guarded architectures rather than raw single‑shot application: (i) architecture and evaluation recommendations for LLM NetOps and AIOps (Bilal et al., arXiv: W7161354925) and a comprehensive survey of LLM‑based network management [W4415071524]; (ii) intent→configuration LLM use and small‑model deployments (Nguyen et al., doi:10.1002/nem.2313); (iii) retrieval/validator approaches that reduce hallucination in other infra domains (e.g., RAG for IaC and medical RAG studies [W4401857375], doi:10.2139/ssrn.6608518); (iv) verifier‑guided IaC repair architectures (TerraFormer / W7124141852). We used these verified sources to justify a paired, validator‑aware experimental design rather than a simple leaderboard. All cited records are verified and archived in the literature record list accompanying the execution manifest.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design: The preregistration (CAND‑2026‑002) was completed before any model calls and is archived in the artifacts. Key preregistered elements: adapter_family=hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model=gpt‑5‑mini; paired design with two conditions (Baseline: Direct‑apply; Guarded: deterministic validator + ≤1 deterministic LLM repair); task_count=400 unique intents; episode_count=800; maximum_model_calls=800; generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate" with independent_condition_generation=false. Rationale for shared_initial_candidate: it isolates validator+repair as the only differing intervention by generating a single initial candidate per intent and sharing that candidate across both conditions; the Guarded arm differs from Baseline only if the deterministic validator rejects the shared candidate and a deterministic repair produces a different accepted candidate. Execution and logging: run executed autonomously; preserved prompts, provider calls, model outputs, adapter logs, per‑task scoring JSONs, and SHA‑256 artifact hashes (see execution_manifest). Scoring and operational failure definition: automated emulator checks measured reachability and policy conformance; an episode was scored as a failure if the applied change produced reachability loss or policy violation as recorded by the emulator scorer (per‑task scoring JSON archived). Analysis plan: primary estimand was the paired difference in operational failure proportion P(failure|Direct‑apply) − P(failure|Guarded); planned tests: McNemar exact two‑sided and 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10k resamples, seed=1729). All analysis code and seeds are archived.
sections.results: Execution summary: run start 2026‑08‑24T21:08:22Z, complete 2026‑08‑24T21:56:41Z (execution_manifest). Completed episodes: 800 (400 unique intents × 2 conditions); model_calls_used=400 (one shared initial generation per intent); no infrastructure failures recorded. Primary confirmatory outcome: every paired intent succeeded operationally in both conditions: n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Expressed as rates: baseline_success_rate=400/400=1.0, guarded_success_rate=400/400=1.0. Paired difference (Guarded − Baseline) = 0.00. Bootstrap (percentile, 10k resamples, seed=1729) 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00]. McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.0. Validator and repair activity (artifact‑grounded): validator_reject_count = 0; deterministic_repair_calls_invoked = 0; therefore Guarded never applied an alternative candidate in this run. Deterministic reconciliation: provider_call_audit in the execution_manifest records stage_counts={"shared_initial_generation":400} and condition_counts={"shared":400}, confirming the shared candidate generation policy. Representative preserved shared candidate response hashes: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 f8de4d6e...abfaf), execution/responses/task-000100-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 68758226...2c9c), execution/responses/task-000400-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 bf23fccd...96d). All per‑task scoring JSONs and provider_call traces are archived with paths and SHA‑256 hashes in the execution_manifest.
sections.discussion: What the run demonstrates and what it does not. The run documents a reproducible boundary case: for the selected 400 intents, the model+adapter produced a shared candidate that the deterministic validator accepted every time; hence Guarded and Baseline were identical for all pairs. This is an artifact‑grounded outcome (validator_reject_count=0) and arises from two interlocking design choices: (1) the task set and its difficulty under the chosen emulator/validator, and (2) the preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation=false). Consequently, the primary inferential machinery (McNemar, bootstrap CI) is mathematically correct but uninformative about validator efficacy in harder settings because no discordant pairs occurred. The archived artifacts permit two immediate, artifact‑based interpretations: (A) under the documented task distribution and adapter, gpt‑5‑mini produced operationally acceptable configurations for the shared candidate policy; (B) because the validator never rejected, we cannot infer whether the validator would have prevented failures on harder or adversarial intents. Reviewer requests and what we can and cannot provide from artifacts: Reviewers asked for positive controls demonstrating scorer/validator sensitivity. No injected failing tasks or external positive‑control runs are present in the archived execution manifest, so we cannot manufacture that evidence post hoc. We therefore preserve this as an unresolved empirical limitation rather than inventing controls. Reviewers also requested release of the exact intent corpus and emulator configuration: these artifacts are present in the execution_manifest (task_manifest.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and per‑task scoring JSONs; the execution_manifest contains paths and SHA‑256 hashes for every preserved file (referenced throughout this paper). Operational implications: a single single‑model, single‑adapter, shared‑candidate run with zero validator activity documents that for some task subsets and generation semantics, an LLM+adapter can produce readily acceptable outputs in a sandbox emulator. This should not be generalized to production. Next steps informed by artifacts (no fabrication): (i) rerun with independent_condition_generation=true so Baseline and Guarded receive independently sampled candidates (preregistered alternative), (ii) include injected failing intents (positive controls) to validate scorer sensitivity, (iii) expand task difficulty and vendor/device diversity, and (iv) measure validator rejection frequency and repair success in settings where the validator fires. These follow‑on steps are described as required future work; the current artifacts do not contain them.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑002) comparing Direct‑apply and a deterministic validator+≤1 repair intervention on 400 intent→configuration tasks using gpt‑5‑mini and a hosted NetOps adapter. Observed result: zero operational failures in both arms and zero validator rejections. Because the preregistered shared_initial_candidate policy produced identical applied changes across conditions, the experiment reports a transparent boundary case rather than evidence about validator efficacy in broader settings. We publish the full preregistration, execution manifest, scoring artifacts, provider_call traces, and analysis scripts (all paths and SHA‑256 hashes are recorded in the execution_manifest) so follow‑on work can vary generation semantics, inject controls, and extend the evaluation to more adversarial and production‑like conditions. We close with the explicit, artifact‑grounded recommendation: paired designs for validator evaluation should either (A) sample independent candidates per condition or (B) include injected failing controls when using shared‑candidate semantics—both choices were prespecified alternatives in the archived preregistration and are natural next steps given the observed outcome.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock. Human role: the Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary and tool permissions pre‑lock; no human manually edited, rewrote, reorganized, shortened, extended, or selectively changed manuscript technical content after the lock. LLM(s) used: gpt‑5‑mini (as recorded in the preregistration and execution artifacts). Adapter/orchestration: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt and system instructions: preserved in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865) and in the frozen master prompt bundle supplied with the run. Prompting strategy and generation semantics: preregistered with independent_condition_generation=false and generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate" (i.e., one shared initial candidate per intent, both conditions start from the same generated candidate). Code/experiment generation framework: autonomous internal generators and the hosted adapter produced harnesses; all generated code, prompts, tool calls, model outputs, scoring JSONs, and logs were archived with SHA‑256 hashes in execution_manifest. Permitted tools and capabilities: hosted model API (OpenAI hosted for gpt‑5‑mini), sandboxed emulator replicas assembled from public topology examples, and a deterministic validator implementing generate_validate_repair_v1 limited to one LLM repair call per failing validation. Preregistration/freeze: preregistration CAND‑2026‑002 was completed and frozen prior to any model calls (documented in artifacts). Autonomous literature verification, experiment execution, and analysis were performed by the autonomous researcher; artifacts and verification records are archived. Technical restarts or deviations: execution_manifest records no infrastructure restarts that altered the scientific design; model_calls_used=400 ≤ maximum_model_calls=800. Pre‑lock development: prior collaborative infrastructure development and rehearsals occurred but were not used as empirical evidence for this final run; the preregistration forbade importing pre‑lock experimental outcomes. Deterministic reconciliation: the execution manifest and analysis_results confirm provider_call_audit: stage_counts={"shared_initial_generation":400} and condition_counts={"shared":400}, confirming the shared initial candidate design and that no per‑condition generation occurred. The Research Director retained oversight only for pre‑lock choices; all research question selection, preregistration finalization, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting were autonomous after the lock. Full archived artifacts, hashes, and analysis scripts are available in the execution_manifest referenced by this submission.
limitations: Single‑model and single‑adapter run (gpt‑5‑mini with hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Results do not generalize across models, adapters, or orchestration stacks.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation (independent_condition_generation=false) made Baseline and Guarded identical in this run: validator_reject_count=0 and deterministic_repair_calls_invoked=0, rendering the intervention inert for the observed sample.
Task set scope: the 400 intents were assembled from public/synthetic sources; they may underrepresent production complexity and adversarial inputs.
No injected positive controls were present in the archived artifacts to empirically demonstrate scorer/validator sensitivity; this prevents ruling out scorer false negatives for some failure modes.
Emulator fidelity and absence of live hardware mean external validity for production deployments is limited; vendor/device idiosyncrasies were not exhaustively tested.
Because all paired outcomes were concordant (all successes), inferential conclusions about validator efficacy for rarer high‑impact failures are not possible from these artifacts alone.
